files.lesson.md: --- order: 15 unit: volume node: AC9M8M02 n2 uses: [AC9M8M02 n1] title: Prism problems summary: "The volume of any right prism is the area of its end (the cross-section) times its length: V = Ah. Work backwards to find a missing length: divide the volume by the area of the end. Give the answer in the units the problem needs." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "A farmer needs a water trough that holds 500 L, a builder orders concrete in cubic metres, a pool needs filling. Each is a prism problem, often run backwards." connection: pool-dose # data/connections/maths.yml app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8306 url: http://127.0.0.1:8306/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: prism.yml#explain-pic, caption: "A triangular prism: the end is ½ × 4 × 3 = 6 cm², so 5 layers make 30 cm³." } explainClip: query: { code: "@prism.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "End area times length" say: "Any prism: the area of the end, times the length." clip: - caption: { text: "The end is a triangle: half of 4 by 3, so 6 cm².", say: "The end is a triangle, six square centimetres." } - wait: 900 - caption: { text: "Each extra centimetre adds another 6 cm³.", say: "Each extra centimetre adds another six." } - click: Make the height bigger - click: Make the height bigger - click: Make the height bigger - click: Make the height bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "= 30" } - wait: 1500 --- A **right prism** has the same cross-section (its end, or base) all the way along. ## Predict: how deep? ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a depth from a capacity shows whether they convert litres to cubic metres and divide by the base area." check: type: predict q: "A tank has a base 4 m by 3 m and holds 36 000 L when full. How deep is it?" options: ["3 m", "3000 m", "12 m", "0.3 m"] actual: "3 m. 36 000 L = 36 m³. The base is 4 × 3 = 12 m², so the depth is 36 ÷ 12 = 3 m." ``` Change the litres to cubic metres first. ## Run: build the tank ```step stage: run insight: "Building a tank to a capacity shows the depth that a base of 12 m² needs." try: { playground: board, starter: "prism.yml#run", height: 600 } check: { type: board, text: "Build the 4 m by 3 m tank that holds 36 000 L. Was your prediction right?", when: "l = 4 and w = 3 and c = 36000", explain: "36 000 L = 36 m³ = 12 m² × 3 m." } ``` Here's the rule the tank was using. For every right prism, $$V = A \times h$$ where $A$ is the area of the end and $h$ is the length (or height) of the prism. Find $A$ with the right area formula for the end: a rectangle, a triangle, or a composite shape. To find a missing length, work backwards: $h = V \div A$. Convert units before you start, so every length is in the same unit. ## Investigate: the end, then the length ```step stage: investigate insight: "Any prism is end area times length (Mia uses l × w × h on a triangle); only the end's own measurements count." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A triangular prism's end has legs 5 cm and 4 cm (a right angle between them). The prism is 9 cm long. What is its volume in cm³?" answer: 90 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["180", "The end is a triangle: half of 5 × 4."] explain: "A = ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 cm², so V = 10 × 9 = 90 cm³." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#mia" text: "Mia finds the volume of a triangular prism. Click the line where her working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: prism-lwh-always explain: "Line 2: l × w × h is for a rectangular box. Any prism is the area of its end times its length: ½ × 3 × 4 × 10 = 60 cm³." - check: type: question q: "The end of a triangular prism is a right triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Which do you need for its area?" options: ["The 3 cm and 4 cm sides (they meet at the right angle)", "All three sides", "The 5 cm side and the length", "Only the 5 cm side"] answer: 0 feedback: [null, "The longest side is not used in ½ × base × height here.", "The 5 cm side is not a height.", "One side cannot give an area."] explain: "The two legs are a base and its perpendicular height: ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²." ``` ### Any prism Here is the routine. ```worked A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12\ \text{cm}^2 :: Find the area of the end with its own formula. V = A \times h = 12 \times 10 = 120\ \text{cm}^3 :: Times the length of the prism. h = V \div A :: To find a missing length, divide the volume by the end's area. ``` Now try one. ### Find the mistake Read Mia's working. What shape is the end? ### What you need ## Modify: work backwards ```step stage: modify insight: "Missing lengths from volumes and capacities, and a prism whose end is a composite shape." try: { playground: board, starter: "prism.yml#triangle", height: 600 } tasks: - starter: "prism.yml#triangle" hint: ["The end's area times the length must be 60.", "Try legs 3 and 4 (end area 6)."] check: { type: board, text: "Make a triangular prism with a volume of 60 cm³.", when: "v = 60", explain: "For example legs 3 and 4 (6 cm²) and length 10, or legs 4 and 5 (10 cm²) and length 6." } - check: type: number q: "A box has a volume of 240 cm³ and a base 8 cm by 6 cm. How tall is it, in cm?" answer: 5 tolerance: 0 explain: "A = 8 × 6 = 48 cm², so h = 240 ÷ 48 = 5 cm." - starter: "prism.yml#pool" hint: ["48 000 L = 48 m³.", "The base is 6 × 4 = 24 m²."] check: { type: board, text: "A pool is 6 m by 4 m and must hold 48 000 L. Set its depth.", when: "c = 48000", explain: "48 m³ ÷ 24 m² = 2 m." } - check: type: number q: "A concrete step is 2 m long. Its end is an L made of two rectangles: 0.6 m by 0.3 m and 0.3 m by 0.5 m. How many m³ of concrete does it need?" answer: 0.66 tolerance: 0 explain: "The end is 0.18 + 0.15 = 0.33 m², so V = 0.33 × 2 = 0.66 m³." ``` ### A volume of 60 ### Find the height ### Fill a pool ### A composite end ## Practise: prism problems ```step stage: practise insight: "Volume, capacity and a missing length, mixed; using l × w × h on a triangle is the planted slip; the conversion review keeps litres fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "A prism's end has an area of 15 cm² and it is 8 cm long. What is its volume in cm³?" answer: 120 tolerance: 0 explain: "15 × 8 = 120 cm³." - check: type: number q: "A fish tank is 50 cm by 40 cm by 30 cm. How many litres does it hold?" answer: 60 tolerance: 0 explain: "50 × 40 × 30 = 60 000 cm³ = 60 L." - check: type: number q: "A trough is 2 m long, 1 m wide and 0.5 m deep. How many 10 L buckets fill it?" answer: 100 tolerance: 0 explain: "2 × 1 × 0.5 = 1 m³ = 1000 L, and 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 buckets." - check: type: number q: "Review: how many mL does 1.25 L hold?" answer: 1250 tolerance: 0 explain: "1.25 × 1000 = 1250 mL." ``` ### End area times length ### A fish tank ### Buckets ### Review: litres ## Make: a box to order ```step stage: make insight: "Designing to both a base area and a capacity makes the student plan the length from V = Ah." try: { playground: board, starter: "prism.yml#box", height: 600 } hint: ["960 mL = 960 cm³.", "With a base of 80 cm², the height is 960 ÷ 80."] check: { type: board, text: "Design a box with a base area of 80 cm² that holds 960 mL.", when: "A = 80 and c = 960", explain: "The base can be 10 × 8 or 8 × 10, and the height 960 ÷ 80 = 12 cm." } ``` Then explain how you found the height before you moved the slider. ## Make: a pool dose, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "A pool dose runs volume to litres to doses: the box volume in m³, times 1000, then how many lots of 10 000 L." hint: ["Find the volume in cubic metres first.", "1 m³ holds 1000 L."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A backyard pool is 6 m long and 3.5 m wide. Its floor slopes, so use an average depth of 1.2 m. The chlorine label says to add 50 g for every 10 000 L. How many grams do you add?" steps: - ["$V = 6 \\times 3.5 \\times 1.2 = 25.2$ m³", "the pool is a box of average depth: length × width × depth"] - ["$25.2 \\times 1000 = 25200$ L", "1 m³ holds 1000 L"] - ["$25200 \\div 10000 = 2.52$ lots of 10 000 L", "the label doses per 10 000 L"] - ["$2.52 \\times 50 = 126$ g", "50 g for each lot"] picks: - step: 2 q: "How do you change cubic metres to litres?" options: - "Multiply by 1000: a cubic metre holds 1000 L" - "Multiply by 100, like metres to centimetres" - "Divide by 1000" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A cubic metre is 100 × 100 × 100 cm³, not 100.", "Litres are the smaller unit, so there are more of them: multiply."] answer: "126" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["12.6", "That used 100 L to the cubic metre. A cubic metre holds 1000 L."] - ["25200", "That is the litres. The label gives 50 g for every 10 000 L."] - ["2.52", "That is the number of 10 000 L lots. Each lot needs 50 g."] criteria: - "I found the volume in m³ before changing units." - "I changed m³ to litres by multiplying by 1000." - "My answer is in grams and uses the label's rate." explain: "6 × 3.5 × 1.2 = 25.2 m³ = 25200 L, which is 2.52 lots of 10 000 L. At 50 g a lot, that is 126 g." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The pool and the label are made up for the task: for a real pool, follow the real label. Write each step, then type the grams. **Also used in** - **Pool chemicals.** The label doses per 10 000 L, and a pool floor slopes, so people use an average depth. - **Rainwater tanks.** The Bureau of Meteorology says 1 mm of rain on 1 m² gives about 1 L ([Bureau of Meteorology](https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/how/faq-data.shtml)), so a roof's area tells you how many litres a storm could fill. - **Troughs.** A farmer works out the length and the end to hold the litres a trough needs. ```teacher summary: Students use V = Ah for rectangular and triangular prisms, work backwards to missing lengths, and solve capacity problems in context (AC9M8M02, node 2). time: 40 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 10 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 12 min goals: - I can find the volume of any right prism from the area of its end. - I can find a missing length from a volume or a capacity. - I can answer in the units the problem asks for. struggle: Deciding which face is the end. Ask students to point to the shape that stays the same all the way along before they calculate. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need volume and capacity conversions (previous lesson) and composite areas. The one idea: V = A × h for every right prism, where A is the area of the end. The common mistake is using length × width × height on a prism that is not a box (Mia's mistake). The board's prism is built in layers of the end's area; its triangular prism has a right-triangle end. Wider: packaging (the box with the least card for a given volume), and finding dimensions for a required capacity. running: - "Predict: ask what to do with the litres first." - "Run: ask how the depth would change for a bigger base." - "Investigate: ask Mia which face stays the same all the way along." - "Modify: ask for the depth before they move the slider." - "Make: ask for the plan in one sentence." - "Paper: the pool dose is worked in books. Books out; look for m³ to litres before the dose, and the average depth." stuck: - see: A student multiplies three lengths for a triangular prism. ask: What shape is the end, and what is its area? fix: V = area of the end × length. - see: A student mixes m and cm in one problem. ask: Are all your lengths in the same unit? fix: Convert first, then calculate. - see: A student multiplies when working backwards. ask: What times the end's area gives the volume? fix: Divide the volume by the end's area. stretch: A box must hold 1 L. Which whole-number dimensions use the least card? Compare at least four designs. support: Give a printed prism with the end shaded, and a formula card V = A × h. leads: > This completes AC9M8M02. Where it leads: cylinders (Year 9), surface area of prisms, and rates of filling (Rates). exit: q: A tank with a 2 m by 1.5 m base holds 4500 L. How deep is the water? a: 4500 L = 4.5 m³; 4.5 ÷ 3 = 1.5 m. explain: > For any **right prism**, $V = A \times h$: the area of the end times the length. Find the end's area with its own formula (rectangle, triangle or composite). To find a missing length, divide: $h = V \div A$. Convert units first, and answer in the units the problem asks for (mL, L or m³). ```
